correctness.rationale: The exact base-seven cube multiset produces R_1=(19,6,9,0,0,9,6). Each unit-pair lift contributes precisely seven representations of any fixed higher target. For seven-divisible targets the eighteen primitive branches and the singular branch (x,y)=(7u,7v) yield the exact 7^4 R_(n-3) recurrence, separately treating levels one and two. The recurrence implies explicit stable shell values, gives a nonnegative L2-bounded martingale, and yields H_n=594/343+H_(n-3)/7 with limit 99/49. Disjoint valuation shells give the upper and lower power-series tests at exponent three. The normalized energy identity is exact at every finite level. The independent convolution enumerator rechecks every residue through 7^4 and additional exact shell formulas; infinite results rely on the analytic recurrence, not those finite computations.

originality.rationale: The 2021 primary source names and studies the two-cube local representation function but provides neither the exact seven-adic fibre distribution nor the 99/49 limiting collision energy and L^s integrability boundary. The 2003 and 2011/2013 sources classify which classes are representable, not the multiplicities. Published mathematical-record searches for the exact law, collision energy, and moment threshold, together with comparison to accessible related results, found no implication of this complete theorem. The residual possibility of a general local-zeta theorem or inaccessible exact specialization is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: A general p-adic fibre-integrability or local-zeta theorem may imply the threshold after nontrivial specialization; its decisive applicability was not established in the inspected sources.
Some broader analytic-number-theory results could imply an equivalent exact collision energy without naming the fibre law; an unindexed source cannot be ruled out.
A same-object unpublished or otherwise inaccessible calculation could predate this result; no claim of independent priority is made.

value.rationale: The evaluated 99/49 invariant is the limiting normalized number of equal ordered sums of two cubes modulo powers of seven, directly motivated by local variance in arithmetic progressions. Its complete fibre-multiplicity distribution distinguishes residual classes and recursively nested singular strata, going well beyond representability support. The sharp failure of L^3 (despite L^2 finiteness) pinpoints an analytic obstruction for higher-moment arguments; this is a natural arithmetic cutoff rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
